newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep.Leach opposes Clinton's bank fee proposal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep.Leach opposes Clinton's bank fee proposal.

text.p: House Banking and Financial Services Chairman James Leach said Tuesday he opposes President Clinton's proposal to charge state-chartered banks and bank holding companies new fees.

Clinton's budget introduced last week includes new examination fees on state-chartered banks and bank holding companies to raise about $400 million in five years, a statement from Leach, an Ohio Republican, said.
"In reducing the federal deficit, it is my belief that Congress needs to rely less on budget gimmickry and tax increases and more on streamlining and cutting the cost of government," Leach said.

Leach said under the budget proposal, state-chartered banks that currently pay a fee to the states that are primarily responsible for the banks' examinations unfairly would have to pay two examination fees. He also said that banks already cover all Federal Reserve administration costs through placement of sterile reserves with the Board.
"In addition to boosting banking system costs, this proposal is an assault on the nation's historical dual banking system," Leach said.
